items.title: Leg Press or Goblet Squat
items.detail: 3 sets × 8-12 reps — Lower smoothly under control for 2 seconds and press firmly through mid-foot.

items.detail: 3 sets × 8-12 reps — Retract your shoulder blades against the bench and press without locking elbows harshly.

items.detail: 3 sets × 8-12 reps — Draw your elbows downward toward your ribs and pause for one second at the chest.

items.title: Forearm Plank Hold
items.detail: 2 sets × 30-45 seconds — Brace your core and squeeze your glutes; terminate the set before your lower back sags.

items.title: Cool-down
items.detail: Doorway chest stretch for 30 seconds per side

items.title: Cool-down
items.detail: Standing quad and hip flexor stretch for 30 seconds per leg

items.text: Check with a doctor before starting if you have a health condition.
Never compromise posture or lift to absolute failure; finish every working set with at least 1 to 2 clean repetitions in reserve.
Halt any exercise immediately if you experience sharp, stabbing, or radiating joint pain.
The 10-Minute Athletic Anchor: 2 minutes of arm circles and leg swings, 2 sets of 10 bodyweight squats, 2 sets of 8 incline push-ups, and a 4-minute brisk walk.
Leg Press or Goblet Squat → Bodyweight Bulgarian split squat or backpack squat loaded with household books
Machine or Dumbbell Chest Press → Standard floor push-ups or elevated hand push-ups on a sturdy chair
Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up → Doorframe towel rows or bedsheet suspension rows
Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift → Single-leg bodyweight Romanian deadlift reaching toward front foot
Seated Cable Row or Supported Dumbbell Row → Bent-over two-arm row using two full water jugs
Steady-State Aerobic Cardio → Brisk neighborhood outdoor walking, stair pacing, or bodyweight step-touches

progression.text: Calibrate your starting weights. Stop every set with 3 to 4 reps in reserve; prioritize flawless posture over load.
Add 1 to 2 clean repetitions to your exercises or add 5 minutes to Tuesday's aerobic conditioning.
When you hit the top of a rep range across all sets with pristine technique, apply the smallest available weight increment.
Scheduled deload: execute lighter restoration circuits (Session G) to let tendons, ligaments, and the nervous system fully recover.
Resume standard training sessions with refreshed energy; maintain strict 60 to 90 second rest intervals.
Push toward the upper boundary of your rep ranges while ensuring zero technical breakdown on final repetitions.
Peak training density: solidify your performance across all three strength days and complete the optional intervals if recovery allows.
Final consolidation deload: transition back to restorative movements (Session G) and celebrate completing the 8-week athletic foundation block.
